title: Waldo by Wherobots
lede: Waldo, from the Apache Sedona creators at Wherobots, is a geospatial data agent that answers plain-English questions about the physical world with analysis, maps and scheduled pipelines.

points: It finds open and private datasets for a question and checks whether they fit before using them.
It writes and runs the spatial analysis and imagery inference, building maps so each step can be inspected.
Inputs span satellite imagery, geometries, geography data and an organisation's own first-party data.
Finished work ships as a pipeline, dataset or map to an Iceberg-compatible platform such as Databricks, Snowflake or AWS Glue, on a schedule if needed.
It launched in public preview; the team argues general coding agents get spatial relationships wrong and stop at the code.

sections.text: Data teams with a backlog of spatial requests and few specialists able to handle geospatial engineering at regional or planetary scale.
During the preview, Waldo tokens cost nothing extra and users pay only for compute; the launch comment offers $250 in extra credits to Product Hunt users.
